Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "baaf2a3b1c4f4d73cdc9b4c00906cad665984955", "message": "Pin the tables and dispatches the refactor moved", "body": "The mutation gate reported 68.71% on the changed lines: every public method
had a test, but a single example per method leaves a table with an entry
removed, or a match with an arm removed, behaving indistinguishably.

Name the whole of each: every operator SQLite writes as punctuation, every
terminal each realizer constructs and what kind of token it comes back as,
every witness the MySQL builder's own tables declare, and the rule-to-witness
map PostgreSQL's scanner is checked against.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "5203fe1eec970a4c99e3b2c5e5e10b204547a754", "message": "Pin the tables the mutation gate could still remove entries from", "body": "73.07% after the first pass. Name the rest of what the builders declare:
every witness SQLite's character-class table produces, the terminals MySQL's
default sql_mode will not emit and why, and the parser entry points the
coverage check is measured against.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "87fcfb4fb75e98d3bb34614a3b12f6c2d024a467", "message": "Re-apply php-ai-toolkit at its current release, without the loose set…", "body": "…tings

The toolkit split its rule registrations out of extension.neon into a new
rules.neon. Our phpstan.neon included only the former, so after the update not
one of the 39 toolkit rules was running. It also carried a local copy of the
exception policy, which overrode the one rules.neon now owns. Both are gone:
the configuration is the three baseline includes and level max, and analysis
paths move to the Composer script so the file stays only the toolkit contract.

PHPUnit gains the strictness the current template requires — sealed mock
objects, strict about tests that assert nothing, details on all issues,
unshortened arrays in failure output, indirect deprecations ignored rather
than all of them, and coverage that neither hides untouched files nor honours
ignore metadata. The redundant failOn* attributes go; failOnAllIssues covers
them and opts into issue types later releases add.

Infection moves to the toolkit policy of 80/80 on the whole tree, counts a
timed-out mutant as escaped, and writes a per-mutator report so the escapees
can be read rather than guessed at. Formatting stops walking build/, which is
where those reports now land.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "850391c96ee14d8b2f791205bf3d56439fced3cc", "message": "Set only the strictness every supported PHP version can read", "body": "The three attributes removed here arrived in PHPUnit 12. This package
supports PHP 8.1, where PHPUnit 10.5 resolves, refuses the configuration
outright, and turns that refusal into a warning — which failOnAllIssues
then makes a red build on three of the five versions CI covers.

Everything else the configuration asks for is understood by every line
from 10.5 up, so the rest stands."}, {"oid": "25ec25eced76eb7eceb9d83b5606eca2c2411c82", "message": "Make every gate a step you can read, and score mutants against a report", "body": "The workflow now says what it runs rather than hiding formatting and static
analysis behind one composer lint, pins every action to the commit it
resolves to, and grants nothing beyond reading the repository.

The version matrix asks whether the suite passes on each supported PHP.
Whether it survives being split across processes is a different question
and does not depend on the version, so the parallel runner is asked once,
on the highest one.

Mutation testing is handed a coverage report generated by the project's own
PHPUnit configuration. Infection's own initial run stops at the first byte
on STDERR and adds stopOnDefect, so one risky test would leave the gate
scoring a near-empty report as though it had scored everything. Memory is
sized for the report rather than the run, which is where it was exhausted
before, and a pull request is scored on the lines it changed against the
bar the toolkit sets for new code."}, {"oid": "44b375b7cde2db5096ece1bf6c0bc72f911bd6ee", "message": "Say which range a choice is made from, not only that one was made", "body": "A test handed a real Faker can only check that something plausible came
out, and a range one short at either end still produces plausible output
every time. Every spelling the three realizers choose between is now
written down, and so is the range each choice was made from, which is what
makes a change to either of them show up as a failing test rather than as
output that still looks fine.

SQLite's character-class samples are the evidence that a compiled profile
covers the tokenizer rather than only the parts a grammar reaches. They
were a table in the middle of the method that consumes them, which is the
one place they could not be checked from; they are their own subject now,
and written out in a test that says what each of them stands for."}, {"oid": "e4c440365499edde5f0077cdb32bba7a3ae6044e", "message": "Refuse a scan that has not got anywhere", "body": "Every one of the three lexers reads a token by moving an offset past it. A
read that leaves the offset where it was has not read anything, and the
loop around it runs forever: the process hangs rather than fails, which is
the one outcome a test can say nothing about.

Each loop now checks that it got somewhere and refuses when it did not, so
a lexer that cannot make progress says which offset it is stuck at."}, {"oid": "1f3b4738d313801de994691a76f2c41b3b74d62b", "message": "Merge tokens without an index that could run away, and time the gate", "body": "Joining WITH ROLLUP walked an index it also spliced under, which is the one
shape of loop a change to the arithmetic turns into a hang rather than a
failure. It reads the tokens once now and writes the joined ones out.

The mutation timeout is measured rather than assumed. A mutant that removes
a constraint from a generation plan does not hang — the derivation step
limit still stops it — but it walks a far larger derivation on the way, and
those runs take longer than the bar the timeout was set at. Reporting them
as escaped said something about the clock rather than about the tests."}, {"oid": "f7f358331669d74a7da75e542e5ff6092884b03a", "message": "Say what the profile builder touches, and stop covering what is not s…", "body": "…ource

A fixture is not a coverage target: declaring one as used is a warning of
its own, which under the strict configuration is a failed run. The builder
test says it uses the samples it now reads them from."}, {"oid": "805055c907c7927bc8f550a38be17b89ed578b74", "message": "Make the lexical samples their own subject, in all three dialects", "body": "Each builder held a table of the SQL that shows a terminal being lexed,
written out in the middle of the method that consumes it — the one place it
could not be checked from. Each is now its own subject, and written out in
a test that says what every entry stands for.

That is what a compiled profile rests on: the evidence that a terminal can
be produced, and that reading it goes through the parts of the lexer the
profile claims to cover. A sample quietly disappearing left nothing to
fail, which is exactly what the mutation gate was reporting."}, {"oid": "b3d1feedf3be31f7743ca0ade0350fef98a13632", "message": "Ask static analysis the same question on every run", "body": ""}, {"oid": "5cbed4662944b23320ff761782a4f20b9bf9f5d9", "message": "Say what each terminal is spelled as, and bound the search for an ope…", "body": "…rator"}, {"oid": "4a2aefa85198510da8e59c25bc43171299368766", "message": "Make reading input end, and say what each lexeme is read as", "body": ""}, {"oid": "12d23f655a39553146bce72fe6f727c751f7f431", "message": "Merge branch 'feat/ci-scope-pr-triggers' into feat/php-ai-toolkit-sql…", "body": "…-faker"}, {"oid": "c46b03771101de83b339d087d464758120e10956", "message": "Declare what the new tests read, and stop claiming a fixture is covered", "body": "The coverage run is strict about metadata, so a test that touches a
class it has not named is an error rather than a note. Two kinds of that
error crept in with the new tests.

The profile builder tests read the lexical sample catalogues to decide
what a profile should contain, and had not said so. Name them.

The lexer test drives a scanner that exists only under tests, and had
named it as used. A fixture is not in the measured source, so there is
no coverage record to attach it to and the run rejects the claim. Drop
it; the classes it does cover are still listed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "581e4dc50ab735fa94f731fd8a3f2be7bf7d030a", "message": "Read the catalogue back, rather than trusting it was written", "body": "The catalogue is the evidence the generator stands on: every terminal it
may write, the text that was observed to lex into it, and the upstream
scanner rule or lexer state that text reaches. Everything downstream
believes it. Nothing until now read one back.

The tests reached the builders only through the failure paths, so the
catalogue those builders assemble was exercised without being examined.
A sample could lose a token from what it claims to read as, a witness
could lose the rule it is the only evidence for, and an identifier could
lose the prefix that tells a reader which engine and which kind of
witness it is, and every test still passed.

Read the assembled catalogue: the parser modes and their units, the one
unit per scanner rule and per mode, the samples with their text, tokens
and units, and the keyword, lookahead and punctuation witnesses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "ff45f360bfbad80914aaa13f3a0958f1e4af47db", "message": "Let every PHP version run under the strict settings its PHPUnit accepts", "body": "The five PHP versions this package supports resolve four different
PHPUnit majors, and one configuration file had to serve all of them. A
setting any one major rejects makes the file invalid there, so the file
could only ever hold what the oldest accepts -- which meant three strict
settings the toolkit asks for were set on no version at all: complete
arrays in failure output, deprecations narrowed to first-party code, and
mock objects that cannot still take a call nobody planned.

Give each major the file written for it and name that file in the job
that installs it. The settings now apply wherever the major supports
them, rather than nowhere.

Sealing mocks is the one that needed the tests to change. A sealed mock
is one that cannot answer a call it was never told about, and PHPUnit's
way of sealing it does not exist on the older majors this package still
runs on. So the doubles that were verifying calls are now written out:
each records what it was asked, and the test reads that afterwards
instead of describing it in advance. That says the same thing, reads
more plainly, and holds on every major.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "e8b57d9fe93b6803cae0d8ff80708aa3aebf80b6", "message": "Take the review's shape for the workflow, and gate the PHP floor", "body": "Seven things the review asked for.

The explanations written into the workflow come out; the steps say what
they run and that is enough.

The version matrix ran the suite in one process and a second job ran it
split across processes. Only the split one is kept: it answers what the
single-process run answered and the coupling question as well, so
running both was paying twice for one answer.

Static analysis was a job of its own next to a lint job that only
checked formatting. They are one job now, with a step each.

The mutation job generated a coverage report before calling Infection.
Infection runs its own initial tests and builds what it needs, so the
step is gone along with the flags that pointed at its output.

Choosing the PHPUnit configuration was spread across the workflow, which
meant a local run got whichever file was default. A small script answers
which configuration the installed major can read, and every phpunit and
paratest call asks it.

PHPStan's paths were listed on the Composer command. They belong to the
analysis, so they are in the configuration file and the command is just
the command.

Nothing checked that the code fits the PHP version the package claims to
support. PHPCompatibility does, as a step beside the others. It is the
10.0 pre-release rather than the six-year-old stable, because the stable
does not know PHP 8.1: it read every enum method as a plain function and
every namespace holding the word sqlite as the removed extension. One
place still needs telling: a table of observed SQL holds '0x10' as the
text a database lexer reads, which is not PHP comparing a string as a
number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "c536934850d3120710da986bc92487b7ef907c67", "message": "Give the grammar namespace the four responsibilities it actually has", "body": "Thirty-eight classes sat in one namespace, which is what TreeGuard was
reporting: a directory that large is not a unit of anything, it is where
files go when nobody decides where they belong.

They divide cleanly, and the divisions are the ones the code already
works in. Model holds the grammar itself -- rules, productions, symbols
-- and knows nothing about walking it. Walk derives a sentence from that
model and is the only part that can fail for want of a production.
Lexical is the separate business of what a dialect spells things with,
which the model never asks about. Source reads upstream grammar files
and turns them into a model, and nothing else depends on where a grammar
came from.

The generated AST caches hold serialized models, so the class names
recorded in them are rewritten to match; two files reached resources
through a relative path that is one level longer now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "8dbd873fd33d940e0424bfe4b8df99df35a8d8c3", "message": "Ask one collaborator which productions a walk may still take", "body": "Three separate things can close a rule down to nothing during a walk: an
alternative that cannot terminate, a plan naming a shape none of them
match, and a first step that was asked for output when the only
alternative produces none. Each was inline in the derivation loop, each
with its own refusal, and the loop was carrying all three on top of the
walking it exists to do.

They are one question -- which productions remain open here -- and it is
now asked of one collaborator. Two of the three derivations work over
the same grammar model and share it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "3c9cc1bc088001de40bf43a21c684b81f7604145", "message": "Let a MySQL provider be about one kind of thing", "body": "One provider carried fifty-eight methods and seven hundred lines, which
is what LocGuard was reporting. They are not fifty-eight variations of
one idea: some name a statement to send a server, some name a value to
write into one, and some name a fragment a statement is assembled from.
A caller looking for "how do I generate a literal" had to read past
every statement kind to find out.

Three providers now, one per kind, and MySqlProvider builds all of them
against the version it was asked for. Nothing changes for a caller: it
still adds one provider and reaches every method through the generator,
because each of the three registers itself the way the original did.
Each also stands up on its own, so a test can hold the one it is about.

Standing them up needed the three steps every provider repeated to get a
generator -- resolve the version, load its grammar, generate against it
-- so those are a named constructor now rather than copied per provider.

Two tests seeded the generator before building the provider, which made
the number of draws construction happens to take part of the fixture,
and two more drew from the same generator between the two generations
they compare. Both now seed where the comparison starts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "b4cbffe6397523bbf54b043c5bedac6660e78d70", "message": "Split the PostgreSQL provider the same way", "body": "Same finding as the MySQL one and the same division: statements to send
a server, values to write into them, fragments they are assembled from.
PostgreSqlProvider builds all three, so a caller still adds one provider
and reaches everything through the generator.

The syntax fuzz target reaches for both a whole statement and one
particular kind, so it holds the facade and the statement provider
rather than pretending one of them answers both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "2e87244c2f1553a462010ef1b71f5a6c31326ccd", "message": "Separate gathering the evidence from accounting for it", "body": "Building a MySQL lexical catalogue was one method of a hundred and
eighty lines at complexity twenty-nine, and it was doing two unrelated
jobs. One is gathering evidence: the profile's symbol and function
tables name most terminals, a sample table names the ones a table cannot
express, and some are witnessed by being punctuation or a parser entry
rather than by example. The other is accounting: deciding which lexer
state each piece of evidence reaches, and refusing a catalogue that
leaves a state unreached.

They are separate now, and the sample table is separate again from the
handful of samples whose presence depends on what states a version
declares -- a version that reads a dollar sign as a quote needs a
different sample than one that reads it as a name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "0731f7412f769e6b047e6d1a3bfbb3a84689dbc6", "message": "Load a dialect's grammar once per caller, and say which tests are slow", "body": "Splitting the providers left each of them loading the grammar for
itself, so building the facade loaded the same grammar four times. The
facade hands the one it built to the three it registers; a provider used
on its own still builds its own.

A test that loads a whole SQL grammar and derives a statement from it is
not a small test, and the configuration gives a small test one second.
They say so now, rather than being reported as risky whenever the
machine is busy enough for a second not to be enough.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "5d7fc3cc679dac117945f3987043fe51038891fa", "message": "Point every caller at the provider that answers it", "body": "Splitting the MySQL and PostgreSQL providers moved methods off the class
the fuzz targets and harnesses were holding, so each now holds the one
it actually asks: the facade where it asks for a whole statement, the
statement provider where it names a kind. One file asked only for
created tables and no longer needs the facade at all.

Two things the matrix found rather than the local run. ParaTest on the
oldest supported PHP has no --max-processes, so the cap is spelled with
--processes, which every line accepts. And a package that keeps a suite
needing a database now names the unit suite in its parallel run, because
the other suite has a job of its own with the services to answer it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "b5334f3db2d2c8f8e11e7a2791e1b6dd1d108dc9", "message": "Make the code say the same thing on every PHP it claims to support", "body": "Merging static analysis into the lint job put PHPStan on the whole
version matrix, and that found three places where the code was written
for the newest supported PHP rather than for the range.

A data set could be given a name, which PHPUnit gained after the version
the oldest leg installs. The names go; the arguments still identify the
set.

Randomness failure was declared as Random\RandomException, a class that
arrived in PHP 8.2, on a package whose floor is 8.1. Declaring the base
class instead is not an option here -- a generic @throws tells a caller
nothing to catch -- so the tag goes: a system with no source of
randomness is not a condition this package asks a caller to handle.

mysqli::execute_query() also arrived in 8.2, so the override attribute
on it is a fatal error on 8.1, and a fuzz helper that called it could
not run there at all. The helper prepares and runs the statement the way
both versions can; the attribute is refused the way the COPY methods
already are, for the same reason and with the reason written down.

The benchmark was still calling a method the provider split moved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "08f5c11c8731d529b22f3dddfecb85ad1ef0f89f", "message": "Keep the docblock in the shape the rule asks for", "body": "Removing a data set name collapsed the block onto one line, which the
single-line rule refuses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "356122a9f00d90b833116469a2bf9014f8917025", "message": "Keep every branch of the stack building on its own", "body": "The provider split happened in sql-faker, so the callers it moved out
from under belong on that branch too, not only on the branches above it.
Every workflow that runs against sql-faker's pull request now has code
it can analyse.

Two more the matrix found. Asking PHPUnit whether a key is in a fixture
set made it treat the set as an array, which it will not do for an
ArrayAccess with a covariant value type; the tests ask the set instead,
which is what they were about. And a test comparing two seeded
generations was spending Faker's provider setup inside the first of
them, so the two started from different states whenever nothing earlier
in the process had warmed it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "400840640a389bc160857809b6c9842cb548a13a", "message": "Point the fuzz targets at the provider that owns each method", "body": "The sql-faker providers were split into literal, fragment and statement
responsibilities, but the downstream fuzz targets still asked the facade
for methods it no longer carries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "11cded0690d5540794716d91eb8094f960c3dd60", "message": "Name the collaborators the extracted narrowing brought into each test", "body": "Splitting the alternative narrowing out of the derivation gave those tests
a second class to run through, and coverage metadata has to say so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "24712cd01a67d6d887942db68e81d488ff93dd47", "message": "Give the mutation run the time the regrouped package now needs", "body": "Regrouping the grammar moved most of the package, so the changed-lines
gate scores nearly all of it: 4443 mutants, 24 minutes on seven threads.
The runner has three, so the job needs more than the hour it was given.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "c8fdba6bcf7bd52732e0251f77c1b67ce07bd79b", "message": "Let each scan pass consume something before it goes round again", "body": "The action scan leaned on a comment skip reporting whether it had moved,
and the operator scan walked its own index forward, so either could be
asked to go round without consuming anything. The action scan now skips
trivia and then takes one lexeme, and the operator run is measured in one
step. With no way left to hang, the run fits the hour it is given.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "f99fbedbd05cb47485d8b8775aaabe18d7de8a3a", "message": "Name the layers this package has, and clear the source metrics", "body": "Thirteen source-metric violations are gone by saying what each thing is
rather than by relaxing a limit:

- the PostgreSQL and SQLite catalogues are built the way the MySQL one
  already was, by a witnesses class and a coverage class, so a 154-line
  method is now composition and a rule table is a constant;
- each ParserSemantics applies one named constraint per method, which is
  how its own docblock already described the C actions it stands in for;
- both grammar compilers, the token joiner (the spacing rule has a name
  now), the PostgreSQL source reader and the SQLite derivation are split
  along the seams they already had;
- the tokenizer's trivia is its own collaborator, the lexical plans are
  separate from the derivation plans, and each dialect's lexical
  machinery is grouped under Lexical.

Two layer edges ran the wrong way and both were real: the shared grammar
compiler imported the Bison AST out of the MySQL namespace even though
nothing in those 47 files is MySQL-specific, and the shared profile
builder constructed all three dialect builders when it is what bin/build-*
runs. The Bison reader is now part of reading a source, and building a
profile is a Build layer of its own.

Along the way a real bug: PostgreSQL storage parameters were read over a
copy of the statement, so a second SET list never got its values.

deptrac.yaml states the layers, and the lint job checks them along with
the source metrics and the tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "f3c826a8d28b6f6ba212b2eecdcd2c221d28602a", "message": "Keep the architecture cache out of the repository", "body": "Running deptrac wrote its cache beside the config and it was committed
with the rest; the check runs from scratch in CI anyway, so it no longer
writes one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "a54466e386b561441cf6e5d3db97c32449877653", "message": "Let a run of qualifiers and a punctuation mark be settled without goi…", "body": "…ng round

Walking back over the qualification in front of a user variable stepped on
a condition that also had to say when to stop, so a reading of it that never
said stop had nothing else to end the walk. The walk is now taken over the
terminals there are, which bounds it however the condition reads.

Punctuation was answered as a single character that is one of a set, and a
reading of that which asks for either rather than both calls the empty
string punctuation, because every string contains it. It is now answered as
being one of the characters, which the empty string is not.

syntax when removing diagnostic…", "body": "… helper"}, {"oid": "0cf9cc5ab0f12e25ae16c5de96213862e8622351", "message": "test(sql-faker): mutate algorithm code, not the reference declarations", "body": "The three lexical DefinitionFactory files are reference data, like the

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED"}, {"oid": "2dd89bf79675f4e5d6e1b620575448be559a214f", "message": "ci(sql-faker): count timed-out mutants the way Infection does", "body": "Infection treats a timed-out mutant as detected: a mutant that turns a
loop condition into an endless loop cannot be killed by an assertion, and
the framework deliberately keeps generating such mutants
(infection/infection#1133, #2229). The zero-timeout policy with
timeoutsAsEscaped contradicted that, and the remaining timeouts were all
loop-condition mutants whose tests had already been aborted by PHPUnit's
one-second limit; the process then stalled while PHPUnit printed hundreds
of thousands of distinct "Uninitialized string offset" warnings.

Drop timeoutsAsEscaped and maxTimeouts, and bound the mutation job's PHP
memory so runaway mutants end as fatal errors within seconds instead of
holding a thread for the whole timeout.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED"}, {"oid": "016156853d2c900f7ab74fc2267098f1a4732c55", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): make every Deptrac layer one directory", "body": "Grammar keeps only the grammar model and its resources. Everything that

{"number": 281, "title": "refactor(sql-faker): adopt k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit", "state": "CLOSED", "commits": [{"oid": "86b51b192b936ce784346b456df1b486a0e85b31", "message": "build(sql-faker): analyse with php-ai-toolkit instead of the local rules", "body": "phpstan-custom-rules only covered the test-shape and comment rules this
project grew for itself. php-ai-toolkit carries those same rules plus the
contract, exception and documentation rules the project has no equivalent
for, so the package now depends on the toolkit and the local rules package
is gone from its requirements.

Checked-exception analysis comes with it: an exception outside the unchecked
families must now be caught or declared, and a @throws tag that is never
thrown is reported. The AI error formatter and the AI test reporter are
registered so that agent runs and human runs read the same results, and
Infection is told to disable extensions so the reporter cannot make every
mutant look killed.

The two ignoreErrors entries that hid line comments in the fuzz targets are
dropped rather than carried over; those comments sit inside catch blocks and
array literals, which the toolkit's comment rule allows outright.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "e3fa47395deb37c05d84dad3c49ef14c12bd7d4c", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): let the fuzz harness own its dialect checks", "body": "Each of the three fuzz targets carried the same three jobs in one class:
turn corpus bytes into a seed, generate a statement, and decide whether the
server's rejection was a grammar defect or a gap the fuzz run cannot avoid.
The last two were private methods, so the interesting decision — which
SQLSTATEs a schema-less run is allowed to hit — was reachable only through
the target's __invoke().

The seed derivation is identical in all three and is now CorpusSeed. The
dialect decision moves to MySqlSyntaxCheck, PgSyntaxCheck and
SqliteSyntaxCheck, each with a verify() that states in its @throws what a
failure means. PostgreSQL's bracketed-indirection exception was itself a
second decision inside the first, so it becomes PgBracketIndirection.

Two behaviours changed rather than moved. The empty catch around the plain
ROLLBACK swallowed a failure that left the connection in an unknown state;
it now reports on stderr, as does the savepoint rollback that precedes it.
The Error raised for an unexpected rejection now chains the PDOException it
came from, so the driver's own message survives in the fuzzer's report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "8bfb6161b1d5789c881a5ff9dc843b839f030630", "message": "style(sql-faker): expand one-line PHPDoc and apply the wider fixer set", "body": "The toolkit reports a PHPDoc block written on a single line: a tag crammed
onto the same line as its delimiters is easy to miss when reading and easy
to drop a second tag from when editing. Every such block in src and tests is
rewritten with /** and */ on their own lines.

The rest is the new PHP-CS-Fixer set applying itself — single-quoted
strings, alphabetically ordered imports, imported global classes and
functions, and trailing commas in multi-line calls. No behaviour changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "2be765e243e249f606a6060c7652b782d5d6a98a", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): make grammar failures recoverable, not programme…", "body": "…r errors

The generators and grammar parsers reported every failure as a
LogicException, and LexicalException extended one too. That put "this
grammar file declares no rules", "this rule cannot be realized" and "this
SQL did not round-trip" in the same family as a violated precondition —
failures a caller is told to fix rather than handle. sql-faker reads Bison
and Lemon grammars that ship with the servers it targets and tokenizes SQL
it was handed, so all three are runtime conditions.

LexicalException now extends RuntimeException, and two new types carry the
rest: GrammarParseException for source text that yields no rules, and
GenerationException for a grammar that cannot derive a statement. Both are
recoverable, so a caller generating from a grammar it did not author can
catch them without also swallowing its own bugs.

The wording moves onto the exceptions as named constructors. The same eight
messages were spelled out across the MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite
generators, twice with wording that had drifted apart: SQLite named the
empty rule where the others did not, and MySQL said "derivation plan" where
the others said "generation plan". Both now report the more useful form.

Precondition guards are untouched: GenerationPlan, Grammar and
RandomStringGenerator still raise InvalidArgumentException when a caller
passes an empty rule name or an empty catalog, because those are defects at
the call site.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "509ce33dd7c6b1fcf358c44dd874241cb0b38ee9", "message": "test(sql-faker): assert behaviour instead of shape", "body": "The toolkit rejects four habits the suite had picked up, and each one hid a
test that could not fail for the reason it claimed to.

Twelve cases expected an InvalidArgumentException or a LogicException from a
precondition guard: an empty rule name, an empty lexeme catalog, a zero-part
hostname. Those are defects at the call site, so the test only asserted that
broken input breaks. They are deleted; the guards they poked at stay.

Fifteen more asserted a class implements an interface or extends an
exception, which the engine already guarantees and no change to the class
body can break. Deleted too, along with the three-line variant that checked
the same thing for all three dialect lexers. PgGrammar::load() and
SqliteGrammar::load() kept their tests but now assert the loaded grammar has
rules, which is what a caller actually depends on.

Seven read method signatures through Reflection to check default argument
values. The contract they were reaching for is that calling with no
arguments matches calling with those values, so they now assert exactly
that, against one re-seeded generator. Two interface tests that asked
Reflection whether an interface is an interface now exercise the contract:
every Symbol reports its own value, and every Bison declaration kind can be
carried by an AST.

Test methods named after constructors are renamed for the behaviour they
pin down, and the anonymous Faker stubs declare the exception they throw.

Three Reflection uses remain in the SQLite generator tests. They read the
private augmented grammar, and they go away when that augmentation becomes a
collaborator with an API of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "159b8bc4462c60861202f1bfd198cf82ddd297fc", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): make the Bison lexer's states explicit", "body": "BisonLexer had twenty-four private methods, and they were private for one
reason: every one of them read and moved $this->pos. Six were cursor
primitives, sixteen were the states of the scan, and the rest were a
lookahead buffer the parser needs. None of them could be reached without
also owning the position, so the interesting rules — what closes a
brace-delimited action, what a prologue does when the file is truncated —
were only observable by feeding a whole grammar file to next().

The position now belongs to SourceCursor, which every state receives as an
argument instead of reaching into. That is what removes the private
modifier; moving the same bodies onto another class would only have replaced
one shared field with a longer parameter list.

Each state is a BisonScanner that declares the character it starts on and
returns the token it read: DirectiveScanner, ActionScanner, TypeTagScanner,
QuotedLiteralScanner, NumberScanner, IdentifierScanner, PunctuationScanner.
BisonScannerChain holds the order, so the lexer dispatches by lookup and no
scanner knows the others exist. BisonTokenStream carries the lookahead, which
keeps the lexer a forward scan that never re-reads a token.

Trivia is not a scanner. Whitespace and comments may sit between any two
lexemes, so modelling them as lexemes would mean every scanner having to
answer "nothing this time" and the lexer looping until one of them did not.
BisonTrivia skips them before dispatch, which is what lets scan() promise a
token rather than a token-or-null, and turns the old recursion through
token() into a single pass. It also owns the one place a slash is not a
comment: inside an action body a slash is division, so recognising a comment
and requiring one are separate operations.

BisonTokenType is renamed BisonLexeme: it names what was read, not a type.

Two failures change shape. Unreadable grammar source now raises
GrammarParseException rather than a bare RuntimeException, and peekN() below
one raises InvalidArgumentException, because asking for the zeroth token
ahead is a defect in the caller rather than in the grammar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "36d2369128f2bd67376c234ed0b0607b88d575b6", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): give the Bison parser one reader per thing it reads", "body": "BisonParser held twenty private methods and three responsibilities: the
order of a grammar file's sections, the argument shape of each of the eight
declaration kinds, and how a rule's alternatives are assembled. They were
private because each one advanced a shared token stream, so `%define` could
only be exercised by handing a whole grammar file to parse().

The eight declaration shapes are eight different grammars — `%expect` takes
a number, `%token` takes names with optional codes and aliases,
`%parse-param` takes a block of host code — so each becomes a
BisonDirectiveReader that answers for its own directive.
BisonDirectiveReaderChain holds the routing, and the reader for directives
this parser has no model for sits last, which is what keeps an unrecognised
directive from swallowing the declarations after it. Where a declaration
ends was decided in four places by one predicate; it is now
BisonDeclarationBoundary, so those four cannot drift apart.

The rules section splits the same way. BisonRuleReader finds the rules,
BisonAlternativeReader reads one rule's alternatives, and the alternative
being read is BisonAlternativeDraft rather than five local variables that
had to be reset at each of the three places an alternative can end — the
place a forgotten reset would have attached one alternative's action to the
next. BisonPreambleReader and BisonStartSymbol carry what is left.

Readers were written as peek-then-consume, and PHPStan reported the result:
having narrowed the peeked lexeme, it could not see that consuming a token
changes it, so four comparisons looked constant. The stream was missing the
operation the readers actually wanted, and nextIf() is it — take the next
token only if it is one of these kinds. Reading a type tag, a token code or
an alias is now one step that cannot look at one token and consume another,
and the coercion those readers repeated moves onto BisonToken as asString()
and asInt().

BisonSymbolType becomes BisonSymbolForm and BisonTokenInfo becomes
BisonTokenDefinition: one records how a symbol was written, the other is a
terminal a %token directive declares.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "763a170656747a3c390fda32f6a19c24a1724fdc", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): read the terminal catalog before trusting it", "body": "LexicalCatalog was two things: the validated catalog its callers ask
questions of, and the reading that turns a decoded resource file into one.
The reading was three private methods and thirty-one throw sites, fourteen
of which raised the same sentence — so a catalog regenerated from a changed
upstream lexer failed with "Invalid upstream lexical catalog shape." and no
indication of which field had moved.

Reading is now LexicalCatalogShape, section by section, with
LexicalWitnessShape for the individual lexing examples and their two
spellings. The two agreement checks are LexicalCoverageCheck, which holds the
partition rule — every unit of the upstream lexer witnessed or excluded,
never both and never neither — and LexicalWitnessCheck, which holds the
rule that the catalog' two halves refer back to each other. LexicalCatalog
keeps only the questions.

The thirty-one messages become LexicalCatalogException, one named
constructor per way the file can be wrong, and the shape failures now name
the field: "Field: coverage.witnessed" rather than the same sentence again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "fbdf9237737dc2f664a842d53d1d8a1803d87877", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): separate writing MySQL lexemes from reading them…", "body": "… back

MySql\LexicalGrammar held two inverse operations. Realization turns a
terminal into SQL; tokenizing turns SQL back into terminals; the class did
both and compared the results, so eighteen private methods belonging to one
side or the other shared a class with no way to reach either alone. Testing
that a run of digits widens from NUM to LONG_NUM at the right magnitude
meant generating a statement that happened to contain one.

MySqlTokenizer now owns reading, MySqlTerminalRealizer owns writing, and
LexicalGrammar owns the round trip that makes the pair worth having. The
tokenizer's rules are separate methods in the order the server applies them,
so the one that depends on what came before it — a hostname is a hostname
because an `@` preceded it — says so in its signature.

Three things the dialects were repeating move to SqlFaker\Grammar.
LexicalProfileSource loads a profile and refuses one that names a different
server than the caller asked for. LexicalKeywordIndex inverts the profile's
terminal-to-spelling map. LexicalException gains a named constructor per way
realization and tokenizing can disagree, each taking the dialect name, so
three copies of the same eight messages become one.

The round-trip message was rendering both token sequences with
JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR. Those sequences come from arbitrary generated bytes, so
the message could fail on exactly the input it exists to report; it now
substitutes what JSON cannot encode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "394c080dc8944ed4c6ec7ada76e755a6447b7657", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): split writing from reading in the other two dial…", "body": "…ects

PostgreSql\LexicalGrammar and Sqlite\LexicalGrammar held the same conflation
MySQL's did: realization turns a terminal into SQL, tokenizing turns SQL back
into terminals, and both lived in one class with thirty-five private methods
between them. Neither half could be exercised without the other.

PgTokenizer and SqliteTokenizer own reading, PgTerminalRealizer and
SqliteTerminalRealizer own writing, and each LexicalGrammar owns the round
trip. PostgreSQL gains a third: the substitutions its parser frontend makes
by looking ahead were spelled out in three places — once when tokenizing,
once when normalizing a derivation, and once when realization had to find the
keyword a substituted token borrows its spelling from. PgLookahead states
that rule once, in the three directions those callers need it.

Both dialects now load their profile through LexicalProfileSource, index
their keywords with LexicalKeywordIndex, and raise LexicalException's named
constructors, so the file-loading, index-building and message-wording that
were written three times are written once.

The SQLite realizer's twenty-three operator terminals were arms of a match
that mapped each to its spelling; they are a table, and are one now. The
STRICT table option keeps a terminal of its own because SQLite spells it as
an ordinary identifier, and the reason is recorded where the constant is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "92a6248a241e15af58968e20a1368484ef212237", "message": "test(sql-faker): name each generation-plan test after the factory it …", "body": "…exercises

The plan factories were tested, but under names that described the grammar
being restricted rather than the method doing the restricting, so nothing
connected a test to the factory it covers. Each is renamed onto its factory.

The lexical factories had no tests at all — twenty-six methods whose whole
job is to name a lexeme kind and carry its bounds. Each now has one, which is
what catches a factory pointed at a target its dialect has no generator for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "3423a38872eacb9b0fdaa004a5e5f9320d705073", "message": "Let each dialect own how its lexer is fetched and read", "body": "LexicalProfileBuilder had grown into one class that knew the upstream URL
layout of three databases, how to read each of their lexers, and how to
write the result. Give each dialect a builder, name the network as a
LexerSource so a test can answer for it, and leave the publishing to a
writer that asks an ArtifactDirectory where a file may be written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "ab16292aa53f2c3eb9e6e4faff98979a23d33d77", "message": "Let a version be a value and a registry answer for the catalogue", "body": "SqlVersion both was one released pair of artifacts and knew where every
released pair is recorded, so nothing could name a pair the record does
not hold. Give the record its own type and leave SqlVersion the value.
GenerationPlan gains the same treatment: its constructor is how a plan is
made, so the invariants it must hold are checked there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "07d8941ce23cac60b5a578111095cd99fdf9a7b2", "message": "Say in the type what a plan refuses, and name the enum for what it holds", "body": "A generation plan guarded its start rule and lexical target at runtime,
which only a caller that was already wrong could ever trip. Declare them
non-empty instead and let the analyser refuse the call. The provider's own
generation policy moves to the plan factory, so no method has to be hidden
to keep it in one place, and StatementType is named for the start rules it
actually lists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "99df5537d125db7d952a479a77addd72f3431745", "message": "Give the derivation walk an owner and let a production answer for itself", "body": "Each generator kept a step counter as a field and reached into it from a
private walk, so the walk could not be run twice or read on its own. Make
the walk an object that owns its count: one for the shared symbol model,
one for MySQL's, and one for SQLite where a symbol Lemon gives no rule to
is a token and each alternative is weighed against finishing the rest.

SQLite's generator also carried every difference between the grammar its
parser declares and the grammar this package generates from. That is a
subject of its own, so it becomes GrammarAdaptation, and the questions it
asked about a production move onto Production.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "ef0c1510ae62adcab087901c00026b8fa1c77507", "message": "Say what each public entry point promises and what it refuses", "body": "Declare the exceptions that escape, and describe the classes and methods a
caller reaches for. The analyser now checks both, so a caller learns what
it has to handle from the signature instead of from reading the body.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "056897d52e502dd4d22f93cfb1dbe39c3c2e26c1", "message": "Cost a grammar once and ask it two questions", "body": "The analyzer relaxed the same fixpoint twice, once counting tokens and once
counting expansions, with the difference spread across four methods. Make
the relaxation a type that is told what a token and an expansion cost.

An unknown symbol is a disagreement between a generated grammar file and
the parser that wrote it, so it is reported at runtime rather than declared
as something every caller must handle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "e67943f454df57c90185ab5bf932480b0af69f00", "message": "Give the Lemon reader, the parser semantics and the alphabet owners", "body": "The Lemon parser held two symbol sets as fields and reached into them from
nine private steps, so what a name meant depended on which step had run.
Give the sets an owner and let a directive reader and a rule reader tell it
what they learned. What each parser enforces outside its grammar becomes a
ParserSemantics of its own, MySQL's grammar answers which of its rules a
requested start rule is grown from, and drawing characters from an alphabet
is named once instead of hidden inside the string generator.

Every public entry point now has a test that names it. sql-faker is clean
under php-ai-toolkit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "48dfc0f8b2e088f45265694fe9f08c1f4495f88d", "message": "Declare what each test uses, and let Infection read the result", "body": "Under strict coverage metadata a test that reaches a class it never named
is reported risky, which is enough to stop Infection before it starts. Name
them. The mutation config also carried both the deprecated test-framework
option and its replacement, which Infection 0.34 refuses outright, so the
two are merged into the key it still accepts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "baaf2a3b1c4f4d73cdc9b4c00906cad665984955", "message": "Pin the tables and dispatches the refactor moved", "body": "The mutation gate reported 68.71% on the changed lines: every public method
had a test, but a single example per method leaves a table with an entry
removed, or a match with an arm removed, behaving indistinguishably.

Name the whole of each: every operator SQLite writes as punctuation, every
terminal each realizer constructs and what kind of token it comes back as,
every witness the MySQL builder's own tables declare, and the rule-to-witness
map PostgreSQL's scanner is checked against.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "5203fe1eec970a4c99e3b2c5e5e10b204547a754", "message": "Pin the tables the mutation gate could still remove entries from", "body": "73.07% after the first pass. Name the rest of what the builders declare:
every witness SQLite's character-class table produces, the terminals MySQL's
default sql_mode will not emit and why, and the parser entry points the
coverage check is measured against.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "87fcfb4fb75e98d3bb34614a3b12f6c2d024a467", "message": "Re-apply php-ai-toolkit at its current release, without the loose set…", "body": "…tings

The toolkit split its rule registrations out of extension.neon into a new
rules.neon. Our phpstan.neon included only the former, so after the update not
one of the 39 toolkit rules was running. It also carried a local copy of the
exception policy, which overrode the one rules.neon now owns. Both are gone:
the configuration is the three baseline includes and level max, and analysis
paths move to the Composer script so the file stays only the toolkit contract.

PHPUnit gains the strictness the current template requires — sealed mock
objects, strict about tests that assert nothing, details on all issues,
unshortened arrays in failure output, indirect deprecations ignored rather
than all of them, and coverage that neither hides untouched files nor honours
ignore metadata. The redundant failOn* attributes go; failOnAllIssues covers
them and opts into issue types later releases add.

Infection moves to the toolkit policy of 80/80 on the whole tree, counts a
timed-out mutant as escaped, and writes a per-mutator report so the escapees
can be read rather than guessed at. Formatting stops walking build/, which is
where those reports now land.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "850391c96ee14d8b2f791205bf3d56439fced3cc", "message": "Set only the strictness every supported PHP version can read", "body": "The three attributes removed here arrived in PHPUnit 12. This package
supports PHP 8.1, where PHPUnit 10.5 resolves, refuses the configuration
outright, and turns that refusal into a warning — which failOnAllIssues
then makes a red build on three of the five versions CI covers.

Everything else the configuration asks for is understood by every line
from 10.5 up, so the rest stands."}, {"oid": "25ec25eced76eb7eceb9d83b5606eca2c2411c82", "message": "Make every gate a step you can read, and score mutants against a report", "body": "The workflow now says what it runs rather than hiding formatting and static
analysis behind one composer lint, pins every action to the commit it
resolves to, and grants nothing beyond reading the repository.

The version matrix asks whether the suite passes on each supported PHP.
Whether it survives being split across processes is a different question
and does not depend on the version, so the parallel runner is asked once,
on the highest one.

Mutation testing is handed a coverage report generated by the project's own
PHPUnit configuration. Infection's own initial run stops at the first byte
on STDERR and adds stopOnDefect, so one risky test would leave the gate
scoring a near-empty report as though it had scored everything. Memory is
sized for the report rather than the run, which is where it was exhausted
before, and a pull request is scored on the lines it changed against the
bar the toolkit sets for new code."}, {"oid": "44b375b7cde2db5096ece1bf6c0bc72f911bd6ee", "message": "Say which range a choice is made from, not only that one was made", "body": "A test handed a real Faker can only check that something plausible came
out, and a range one short at either end still produces plausible output
every time. Every spelling the three realizers choose between is now
written down, and so is the range each choice was made from, which is what
makes a change to either of them show up as a failing test rather than as
output that still looks fine.

SQLite's character-class samples are the evidence that a compiled profile
covers the tokenizer rather than only the parts a grammar reaches. They
were a table in the middle of the method that consumes them, which is the
one place they could not be checked from; they are their own subject now,
and written out in a test that says what each of them stands for."}, {"oid": "e4c440365499edde5f0077cdb32bba7a3ae6044e", "message": "Refuse a scan that has not got anywhere", "body": "Every one of the three lexers reads a token by moving an offset past it. A
read that leaves the offset where it was has not read anything, and the
loop around it runs forever: the process hangs rather than fails, which is
the one outcome a test can say nothing about.

Each loop now checks that it got somewhere and refuses when it did not, so
a lexer that cannot make progress says which offset it is stuck at."}, {"oid": "1f3b4738d313801de994691a76f2c41b3b74d62b", "message": "Merge tokens without an index that could run away, and time the gate", "body": "Joining WITH ROLLUP walked an index it also spliced under, which is the one
shape of loop a change to the arithmetic turns into a hang rather than a
failure. It reads the tokens once now and writes the joined ones out.

The mutation timeout is measured rather than assumed. A mutant that removes
a constraint from a generation plan does not hang — the derivation step
limit still stops it — but it walks a far larger derivation on the way, and
those runs take longer than the bar the timeout was set at. Reporting them
as escaped said something about the clock rather than about the tests."}, {"oid": "f7f358331669d74a7da75e542e5ff6092884b03a", "message": "Say what the profile builder touches, and stop covering what is not s…", "body": "…ource

A fixture is not a coverage target: declaring one as used is a warning of
its own, which under the strict configuration is a failed run. The builder
test says it uses the samples it now reads them from."}, {"oid": "805055c907c7927bc8f550a38be17b89ed578b74", "message": "Make the lexical samples their own subject, in all three dialects", "body": "Each builder held a table of the SQL that shows a terminal being lexed,
written out in the middle of the method that consumes it — the one place it
could not be checked from. Each is now its own subject, and written out in
a test that says what every entry stands for.

That is what a compiled profile rests on: the evidence that a terminal can
be produced, and that reading it goes through the parts of the lexer the
profile claims to cover. A sample quietly disappearing left nothing to
fail, which is exactly what the mutation gate was reporting."}, {"oid": "b3d1feedf3be31f7743ca0ade0350fef98a13632", "message": "Ask static analysis the same question on every run", "body": ""}, {"oid": "5cbed4662944b23320ff761782a4f20b9bf9f5d9", "message": "Say what each terminal is spelled as, and bound the search for an ope…", "body": "…rator"}, {"oid": "4a2aefa85198510da8e59c25bc43171299368766", "message": "Make reading input end, and say what each lexeme is read as", "body": ""}, {"oid": "12d23f655a39553146bce72fe6f727c751f7f431", "message": "Merge branch 'feat/ci-scope-pr-triggers' into feat/php-ai-toolkit-sql…", "body": "…-faker"}, {"oid": "c46b03771101de83b339d087d464758120e10956", "message": "Declare what the new tests read, and stop claiming a fixture is covered", "body": "The coverage run is strict about metadata, so a test that touches a
class it has not named is an error rather than a note. Two kinds of that
error crept in with the new tests.

The profile builder tests read the lexical sample catalogues to decide
what a profile should contain, and had not said so. Name them.

The lexer test drives a scanner that exists only under tests, and had
named it as used. A fixture is not in the measured source, so there is
no coverage record to attach it to and the run rejects the claim. Drop
it; the classes it does cover are still listed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "581e4dc50ab735fa94f731fd8a3f2be7bf7d030a", "message": "Read the catalogue back, rather than trusting it was written", "body": "The catalogue is the evidence the generator stands on: every terminal it
may write, the text that was observed to lex into it, and the upstream
scanner rule or lexer state that text reaches. Everything downstream
believes it. Nothing until now read one back.

The tests reached the builders only through the failure paths, so the
catalogue those builders assemble was exercised without being examined.
A sample could lose a token from what it claims to read as, a witness
could lose the rule it is the only evidence for, and an identifier could
lose the prefix that tells a reader which engine and which kind of
witness it is, and every test still passed.

Read the assembled catalogue: the parser modes and their units, the one
unit per scanner rule and per mode, the samples with their text, tokens
and units, and the keyword, lookahead and punctuation witnesses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "ff45f360bfbad80914aaa13f3a0958f1e4af47db", "message": "Let every PHP version run under the strict settings its PHPUnit accepts", "body": "The five PHP versions this package supports resolve four different
PHPUnit majors, and one configuration file had to serve all of them. A
setting any one major rejects makes the file invalid there, so the file
could only ever hold what the oldest accepts -- which meant three strict
settings the toolkit asks for were set on no version at all: complete
arrays in failure output, deprecations narrowed to first-party code, and
mock objects that cannot still take a call nobody planned.

Give each major the file written for it and name that file in the job
that installs it. The settings now apply wherever the major supports
them, rather than nowhere.

Sealing mocks is the one that needed the tests to change. A sealed mock
is one that cannot answer a call it was never told about, and PHPUnit's
way of sealing it does not exist on the older majors this package still
runs on. So the doubles that were verifying calls are now written out:
each records what it was asked, and the test reads that afterwards
instead of describing it in advance. That says the same thing, reads
more plainly, and holds on every major.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "e8b57d9fe93b6803cae0d8ff80708aa3aebf80b6", "message": "Take the review's shape for the workflow, and gate the PHP floor", "body": "Seven things the review asked for.

The explanations written into the workflow come out; the steps say what
they run and that is enough.

The version matrix ran the suite in one process and a second job ran it
split across processes. Only the split one is kept: it answers what the
single-process run answered and the coupling question as well, so
running both was paying twice for one answer.

Static analysis was a job of its own next to a lint job that only
checked formatting. They are one job now, with a step each.

The mutation job generated a coverage report before calling Infection.
Infection runs its own initial tests and builds what it needs, so the
step is gone along with the flags that pointed at its output.

Choosing the PHPUnit configuration was spread across the workflow, which
meant a local run got whichever file was default. A small script answers
which configuration the installed major can read, and every phpunit and
paratest call asks it.

PHPStan's paths were listed on the Composer command. They belong to the
analysis, so they are in the configuration file and the command is just
the command.

Nothing checked that the code fits the PHP version the package claims to
support. PHPCompatibility does, as a step beside the others. It is the
10.0 pre-release rather than the six-year-old stable, because the stable
does not know PHP 8.1: it read every enum method as a plain function and
every namespace holding the word sqlite as the removed extension. One
place still needs telling: a table of observed SQL holds '0x10' as the
text a database lexer reads, which is not PHP comparing a string as a
number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "c536934850d3120710da986bc92487b7ef907c67", "message": "Give the grammar namespace the four responsibilities it actually has", "body": "Thirty-eight classes sat in one namespace, which is what TreeGuard was
reporting: a directory that large is not a unit of anything, it is where
files go when nobody decides where they belong.

They divide cleanly, and the divisions are the ones the code already
works in. Model holds the grammar itself -- rules, productions, symbols
-- and knows nothing about walking it. Walk derives a sentence from that
model and is the only part that can fail for want of a production.
Lexical is the separate business of what a dialect spells things with,
which the model never asks about. Source reads upstream grammar files
and turns them into a model, and nothing else depends on where a grammar
came from.

The generated AST caches hold serialized models, so the class names
recorded in them are rewritten to match; two files reached resources
through a relative path that is one level longer now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "8dbd873fd33d940e0424bfe4b8df99df35a8d8c3", "message": "Ask one collaborator which productions a walk may still take", "body": "Three separate things can close a rule down to nothing during a walk: an
alternative that cannot terminate, a plan naming a shape none of them
match, and a first step that was asked for output when the only
alternative produces none. Each was inline in the derivation loop, each
with its own refusal, and the loop was carrying all three on top of the
walking it exists to do.

They are one question -- which productions remain open here -- and it is
now asked of one collaborator. Two of the three derivations work over
the same grammar model and share it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "3c9cc1bc088001de40bf43a21c684b81f7604145", "message": "Let a MySQL provider be about one kind of thing", "body": "One provider carried fifty-eight methods and seven hundred lines, which
is what LocGuard was reporting. They are not fifty-eight variations of
one idea: some name a statement to send a server, some name a value to
write into one, and some name a fragment a statement is assembled from.
A caller looking for "how do I generate a literal" had to read past
every statement kind to find out.

Three providers now, one per kind, and MySqlProvider builds all of them
against the version it was asked for. Nothing changes for a caller: it
still adds one provider and reaches every method through the generator,
because each of the three registers itself the way the original did.
Each also stands up on its own, so a test can hold the one it is about.

Standing them up needed the three steps every provider repeated to get a
generator -- resolve the version, load its grammar, generate against it
-- so those are a named constructor now rather than copied per provider.

Two tests seeded the generator before building the provider, which made
the number of draws construction happens to take part of the fixture,
and two more drew from the same generator between the two generations
they compare. Both now seed where the comparison starts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "b4cbffe6397523bbf54b043c5bedac6660e78d70", "message": "Split the PostgreSQL provider the same way", "body": "Same finding as the MySQL one and the same division: statements to send
a server, values to write into them, fragments they are assembled from.
PostgreSqlProvider builds all three, so a caller still adds one provider
and reaches everything through the generator.

The syntax fuzz target reaches for both a whole statement and one
particular kind, so it holds the facade and the statement provider
rather than pretending one of them answers both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "2e87244c2f1553a462010ef1b71f5a6c31326ccd", "message": "Separate gathering the evidence from accounting for it", "body": "Building a MySQL lexical catalogue was one method of a hundred and
eighty lines at complexity twenty-nine, and it was doing two unrelated
jobs. One is gathering evidence: the profile's symbol and function
tables name most terminals, a sample table names the ones a table cannot
express, and some are witnessed by being punctuation or a parser entry
rather than by example. The other is accounting: deciding which lexer
state each piece of evidence reaches, and refusing a catalogue that
leaves a state unreached.

They are separate now, and the sample table is separate again from the
handful of samples whose presence depends on what states a version
declares -- a version that reads a dollar sign as a quote needs a
different sample than one that reads it as a name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "0731f7412f769e6b047e6d1a3bfbb3a84689dbc6", "message": "Load a dialect's grammar once per caller, and say which tests are slow", "body": "Splitting the providers left each of them loading the grammar for
itself, so building the facade loaded the same grammar four times. The
facade hands the one it built to the three it registers; a provider used
on its own still builds its own.

A test that loads a whole SQL grammar and derives a statement from it is
not a small test, and the configuration gives a small test one second.
They say so now, rather than being reported as risky whenever the
machine is busy enough for a second not to be enough.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "5d7fc3cc679dac117945f3987043fe51038891fa", "message": "Point every caller at the provider that answers it", "body": "Splitting the MySQL and PostgreSQL providers moved methods off the class
the fuzz targets and harnesses were holding, so each now holds the one
it actually asks: the facade where it asks for a whole statement, the
statement provider where it names a kind. One file asked only for
created tables and no longer needs the facade at all.

Two things the matrix found rather than the local run. ParaTest on the
oldest supported PHP has no --max-processes, so the cap is spelled with
--processes, which every line accepts. And a package that keeps a suite
needing a database now names the unit suite in its parallel run, because
the other suite has a job of its own with the services to answer it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "b5334f3db2d2c8f8e11e7a2791e1b6dd1d108dc9", "message": "Make the code say the same thing on every PHP it claims to support", "body": "Merging static analysis into the lint job put PHPStan on the whole
version matrix, and that found three places where the code was written
for the newest supported PHP rather than for the range.

A data set could be given a name, which PHPUnit gained after the version
the oldest leg installs. The names go; the arguments still identify the
set.

Randomness failure was declared as Random\RandomException, a class that
arrived in PHP 8.2, on a package whose floor is 8.1. Declaring the base
class instead is not an option here -- a generic @throws tells a caller
nothing to catch -- so the tag goes: a system with no source of
randomness is not a condition this package asks a caller to handle.

mysqli::execute_query() also arrived in 8.2, so the override attribute
on it is a fatal error on 8.1, and a fuzz helper that called it could
not run there at all. The helper prepares and runs the statement the way
both versions can; the attribute is refused the way the COPY methods
already are, for the same reason and with the reason written down.

The benchmark was still calling a method the provider split moved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "08f5c11c8731d529b22f3dddfecb85ad1ef0f89f", "message": "Keep the docblock in the shape the rule asks for", "body": "Removing a data set name collapsed the block onto one line, which the
single-line rule refuses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "356122a9f00d90b833116469a2bf9014f8917025", "message": "Keep every branch of the stack building on its own", "body": "The provider split happened in sql-faker, so the callers it moved out
from under belong on that branch too, not only on the branches above it.
Every workflow that runs against sql-faker's pull request now has code
it can analyse.

Two more the matrix found. Asking PHPUnit whether a key is in a fixture
set made it treat the set as an array, which it will not do for an
ArrayAccess with a covariant value type; the tests ask the set instead,
which is what they were about. And a test comparing two seeded
generations was spending Faker's provider setup inside the first of
them, so the two started from different states whenever nothing earlier
in the process had warmed it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "400840640a389bc160857809b6c9842cb548a13a", "message": "Point the fuzz targets at the provider that owns each method", "body": "The sql-faker providers were split into literal, fragment and statement
responsibilities, but the downstream fuzz targets still asked the facade
for methods it no longer carries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "11cded0690d5540794716d91eb8094f960c3dd60", "message": "Name the collaborators the extracted narrowing brought into each test", "body": "Splitting the alternative narrowing out of the derivation gave those tests
a second class to run through, and coverage metadata has to say so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "24712cd01a67d6d887942db68e81d488ff93dd47", "message": "Give the mutation run the time the regrouped package now needs", "body": "Regrouping the grammar moved most of the package, so the changed-lines
gate scores nearly all of it: 4443 mutants, 24 minutes on seven threads.
The runner has three, so the job needs more than the hour it was given.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "c8fdba6bcf7bd52732e0251f77c1b67ce07bd79b", "message": "Let each scan pass consume something before it goes round again", "body": "The action scan leaned on a comment skip reporting whether it had moved,
and the operator scan walked its own index forward, so either could be
asked to go round without consuming anything. The action scan now skips
trivia and then takes one lexeme, and the operator run is measured in one
step. With no way left to hang, the run fits the hour it is given.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "f99fbedbd05cb47485d8b8775aaabe18d7de8a3a", "message": "Name the layers this package has, and clear the source metrics", "body": "Thirteen source-metric violations are gone by saying what each thing is
rather than by relaxing a limit:

- the PostgreSQL and SQLite catalogues are built the way the MySQL one
  already was, by a witnesses class and a coverage class, so a 154-line
  method is now composition and a rule table is a constant;
- each ParserSemantics applies one named constraint per method, which is
  how its own docblock already described the C actions it stands in for;
- both grammar compilers, the token joiner (the spacing rule has a name
  now), the PostgreSQL source reader and the SQLite derivation are split
  along the seams they already had;
- the tokenizer's trivia is its own collaborator, the lexical plans are
  separate from the derivation plans, and each dialect's lexical
  machinery is grouped under Lexical.

Two layer edges ran the wrong way and both were real: the shared grammar
compiler imported the Bison AST out of the MySQL namespace even though
nothing in those 47 files is MySQL-specific, and the shared profile
builder constructed all three dialect builders when it is what bin/build-*
runs. The Bison reader is now part of reading a source, and building a
profile is a Build layer of its own.

Along the way a real bug: PostgreSQL storage parameters were read over a
copy of the statement, so a second SET list never got its values.

deptrac.yaml states the layers, and the lint job checks them along with
the source metrics and the tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "f3c826a8d28b6f6ba212b2eecdcd2c221d28602a", "message": "Keep the architecture cache out of the repository", "body": "Running deptrac wrote its cache beside the config and it was committed
with the rest; the check runs from scratch in CI anyway, so it no longer
writes one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, {"oid": "a54466e386b561441cf6e5d3db97c32449877653", "message": "Let a run of qualifiers and a punctuation mark be settled without goi…", "body": "…ng round

Walking back over the qualification in front of a user variable stepped on
a condition that also had to say when to stop, so a reading of it that never
said stop had nothing else to end the walk. The walk is now taken over the
terminals there are, which bounds it however the condition reads.

Punctuation was answered as a single character that is one of a set, and a
reading of that which asks for either rather than both calls the empty
string punctuation, because every string contains it. It is now answered as
being one of the characters, which the empty string is not.

#	packages/sql-faker/tests/Unit/SqliteProviderTest.php"}, {"oid": "746069e39827803958d3642ab092f0eced30bf9c", "message": "refactor(sql-faker): reduce fuzzing to container, plan, SQL and database", "body": "The fuzz targets start the database, compile the input into a plan,
generate one statement and prepare it on the server. Each check lists
the errors a schema-less run cannot avoid as a constant with the reason
next to every entry; anything else is a finding for PHP-Fuzzer, and a
lost connection ends the run with status 2. The fuzz code returns to
the Fuzz namespace and needs no tests of its own.

The oracle abstraction, the program-root target with its native
PostgreSQL and SQLite modules, the verification coverage with its
witness store and acceptance rate, the PHP-Fuzzer feature feedback and
the integration tests are removed. Grammar coverage stays an SQLFaker
recorder: a target only decides whether it is on, and the recorder
persists its snapshot every hundred generations and at shutdown.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED"}, {"oid": "2dd89bf79675f4e5d6e1b620575448be559a214f", "message": "ci(sql-faker): count timed-out mutants the way Infection does", "body": "Infection treats a timed-out mutant as detected: a mutant that turns a
loop condition into an endless loop cannot be killed by an assertion, and
the framework deliberately keeps generating such mutants
(infection/infection#1133, #2229). The zero-timeout policy with
timeoutsAsEscaped contradicted that, and the remaining timeouts were all
loop-condition mutants whose tests had already been aborted by PHPUnit's
one-second limit; the process then stalled while PHPUnit printed hundreds
of thousands of distinct "Uninitialized string offset" warnings.

Drop timeoutsAsEscaped and maxTimeouts, and bound the mutation job's PHP
memory so runaway mutants end as fatal errors within seconds instead of
holding a thread for the whole timeout.
